⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 10/10 – Friendship sold separately.

Bought this expecting a decent co-op game. Left questioning how the developers managed to come up with a new gameplay mechanic every 15 minutes.

Every time I thought, "Alright, I get the gameplay loop now," the game basically said, "Cool. Here's something completely different." It somehow keeps throwing fresh ideas at you without overstaying any of them. More games need this level of confidence.

The best part? It actually respects both players. Nobody gets stuck being "the sidekick" holding a flashlight while the other person has all the fun. Both players get cool moments, stupid moments, and plenty of opportunities to accidentally (or intentionally) sabotage each other.

The boss fights are creative, the puzzles are satisfying, and the world-switching between fantasy and sci-fi never gets old. There were multiple moments where my friend and I just stopped for a second and went, "Wait... they actually did this?"

Performance was smooth, the visuals are fantastic, and the soundtrack knows exactly when to hype you up.

Only downside? You need a friend. Steam doesn't sell those yet.

If you enjoy co-op games and somehow skipped Split Fiction, fix that mistake. This is easily one of the best co-op experiences I've played in years.

• Great follow up to It Takes Two, Hazelight really knows how to make the most of the split screen format in how well they can keep adding on creative mechanics every level with constant shifting of perspective. How they pulled off the last hour especially I have no clue, but was incredibly cool

• The side stories were neat too and give more bite sized ideas next to the lengthier main path, though I do wish there were still the more competitive mini-games ITT had as this essentially replaces that

• Visually, Split Fiction is a step up over its predecessor and the set pieces throughout the game are very well done. I had no bugs or performance issues on PC either despite this being on UE5

• I do think the writing is much weaker than the gameplay though (same as ITT more or less), but was fine. Mio and Zoe are likable enough and the ending itself is nice, but it’s fairly predictable from the start and dialogue in general is pretty cheesy

Split Fiction has got to be one of if not the best co-op experiences I've even had in a game. 

It literally has something for everyone, it dabbles with so many forms of puzzles and genres of gameplay.
One moment you're solving a third person puzzle, the next you're on a side scrolling adventure in the middle of a boss fight. I genuinely had a blast with each level, and just when you think you've found your favorite one, the next is just somehow even better and memorable.

The story woven through the game was incredibly well written to progress forwards, with characters you grow to love and feel for. Both of the girls differ substantially in gameplay giving you the experience to play both sides with vastly different mechanics. That's a massive plus for replayability!

I was lucky enough to play this with the person I love who enjoys video games as much as I do, easily made the experience that much better!

Dude, I got to be a farting pig that became a hotdog... literally what other game has that?!

10/10

Split Fiction is one of those rare indie gems that manages to blend clever writing, unique gameplay mechanics, and emotional storytelling into a single unforgettable experience.

The dual-perspective storytelling is brilliantly executed—switching between characters isn't just a gimmick; it's central to the narrative and gameplay. Every choice feels meaningful, and the branching paths actually matter. The dialogue is sharp, witty, and at times surprisingly heartfelt. It’s clear a lot of love went into crafting this world.

Visually, it leans into a minimalist but expressive art style that fits the story's tone perfectly. The soundtrack is subtle but effective, kicking in at the right emotional beats.

If you’re a fan of narrative-driven games like Oxenfree, Night in the Woods, or Disco Elysium, Split Fiction will absolutely scratch that itch.

Highly recommend this one.

🌟 An Absolute Masterpiece! 🌟

Hazelight Studios has done it again! After It Takes Two, I had high expectations, but Split Fiction has completely blown me away. From its breathtaking storytelling to the seamless co-op gameplay, this game is a true work of art.

The level design is insanely creative, the puzzles are engaging, and the emotional depth of the story is simply unmatched. Every moment feels carefully crafted to keep players immersed, whether you're laughing at the hilarious dialogues or feeling the weight of the heartfelt moments.

The co-op experience is flawless, making teamwork feel natural and rewarding. It’s rare to find a game that balances fun, challenge, and emotional impact so perfectly. Hazelight continues to prove why they are masters of co-op gaming.

If you're looking for an unforgettable adventure, Split Fiction is a must-play. No doubt, this deserves to be Game of the Year! Can’t wait to see what Hazelight Studios brings us next. 🎮🔥
